title: Hammer Crusher
model_title: Hammer Mill / Hammer Crusher (Swing Hammers + Grate)

introduction.definition: A hammer crusher (hammer mill) has a rotor carrying many pivoted (swing) hammers. At speed the hammers swing out and strike the feed, throwing it against a breaker plate; the material is then broken further until it is small enough to pass through the grate bars at the bottom. The grate opening controls the top size of the product.
applications: Coal crushing for power plants and cement kilns
key_points: Swing hammers fold back on uncrushable objects
Grate sets the product top size
High reduction ratio in one pass
Not for very hard or abrasive rock
introduction.summary: A hammer crusher (hammer mill) uses swinging hammers on a fast rotor to smash material against a breaker plate; it keeps hitting it until it is small enough to pass through the grate bars below. Used for coal, limestone, clinker and softer materials.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Throughput falls and fines increase with smaller grate openings; moisture causes grate blinding.

wear.title: Wear on the breaker plate, grate and hammer tips
wear.description: The breaker plate takes the direct impact of material thrown by the hammers (purple); the grate bars wear from abrasion as the product is forced through (pink), which widens the openings and coarsens the product. Hammer tips wear too — hammers are turned or reversed to use all four edges before replacement, and replaced in matched-weight sets to keep the rotor balanced.

foundation: Mount on a massive reinforced-concrete foundation or steel structure designed for the crusher's dynamic loads (maker's load data); use anti-vibration mounts where specified.
Allow crane access and lay-down space for liner and wear-part changes.
alignment: Align motor and crusher sheaves or coupling; set V-belt tension to the maker's figure.
Set the closed-side setting (CSS) or gap with the maker's gauge/lead-ball method.
piping: Feed with a controlled feeder (choke or regulated feed as designed); avoid segregated or one-sided feed.
Fit a tramp-metal magnet or metal detector ahead of the crusher and dust extraction at transfer points.
Lubrication system: connect oil supply/return, cooler and filter; check flow and pressure switches.
commissioning: Check lubrication flows and temperatures before starting; run empty to check direction, vibration and current.
Introduce feed gradually; measure product size and adjust the setting; record power draw as a baseline.

remedies: Dry feed or use larger openings

safety: Lock out and block the rotor; flying debris hazard.

video_tutorials.title: Hammer Crusher — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Hammer Crusher.
A hammer crusher (hammer mill) has a rotor carrying many pivoted (swing) hammers.
At speed the hammers swing out and strike the feed, throwing it against a breaker plate; the material is then broken further until it is small enough to pass through the grate bars at the bottom.
The grate opening controls the top size of the product.
Typical applications include coal crushing for power plants and cement kilns; limestone, gypsum and clinker; biomass and recycling.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Housing with Wear Liners, Rotor with Swing Hammers & Shaft.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Hammer Crusher works.
Feed enters at the top.
The swing hammers on the rotor strike the falling lumps.
Material is thrown against the breaker plate and broken again.
Crushed product passes the grate bars.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

The breaker plate takes the direct impact of material thrown by the hammers (purple); the grate bars wear from abrasion as the product is forced through (pink), which widens the openings and coarsens the product.

video_tutorials.title: Hammer Crusher — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Hammer Crusher.
Check vibration and grate blockage.
Inspect hammers and pins for wear; reverse hammers.
Replace hammers in balanced sets, pins, grate bars and liners.
Watch for grate blinding: capacity drops, power rises. Common cause: wet/sticky feed.
Watch for imbalance: vibration. Common cause: uneven hammer wear, lost hammer.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
